single.responseChoice: Every legal relation response and one-shot storage/notification fault is free.

multiple.scope: Global whole-process crash affects every actor. Relation multi-actor uses fixed scripts by cumulative attempt; knowledge one/two parts keep free responses/errors and fault choices. No original KEJ-63/64 domain is substituted or reduced.

relation.commitBarrier: If any actor is committed, the whole JavaScript worker is synchronously blocked; only that actor notify/notify_fail or global crash is legal.

slots.repairOk: Accept exactly the currently anchored unresolved sourceIndex slots.

knowledge.partExecution: Sequential; send/response/commit require the actual inflight part.

traceContract.normalization: Strip module namespaces through the last ::; reject duplicate normalized names; decode ITF #bigint/#map/#set without reordering actions.
traceContract.crash: Global action, actor=-1. Allowed only at reserved/inflight/received/committed boundary and generation < 1. processState=down; knowledge stage=down. Durable values and external calls remain. Relation observational phases and volatile replies retain the last observed snapshot until recovery.
traceContract.recover: actor=-1. Launch a fresh worker/PID over the same SQLite path; processState=up, generation+1, all replies=none. Never construct a store in the observer: read SQLite read-only.
traceContract.relationRecovery: reserved/inflight/received become idle if counts<3, otherwise done/failed. committed becomes done, retaining result/outcome. Existing retry_wait remains and must advance_time. No persisted request or journal count resets.
traceContract.knowledgeRecovery: extract_inflight becomes extract_pending; repair_inflight becomes done with retained repair_reserved, accepted/unresolved and real REPAIR_INTERRUPTED diagnostic. Other phases, initial_requests, extra/protocol budgets, retry_kind, last_request_at and accepted state remain. stage=idle/outcome=none/ready=false in this fixed-clock active-boundary scope.
traceContract.commit: Real SQLite transaction returns. A synchronous bounded test-only file handshake pauses before the first result callback, without production await; stage/phase committed is observable but no notification or settlement has run.
traceContract.notify: notify or notify_fail resumes the synchronous continuation. Knowledge then settles pending/terminal job state; relation terminal commit result already exists. Notifications are not an outbox.
traceContract.settle: Knowledge actor=-1; after recovery, all parts already done and deadline reached. Scheduler completes without provider call.
traceContract.settle_exhausted: Knowledge actor=p; after recovery, initial_requests>0 and extra_requests>=2 or exhausted protocol retry. Mark part done, no provider call, then settle/continue.
traceContract.ready: Knowledge false only at idle waiting for persisted interval/retry/cooldown; recovery does not bypass last_request_at+2000, even when all parts are done. Relation false for retry_wait only.
traceContract.faults: reserve_fail/commit_fail are one-shot storage failures followed by writable failure-state persistence; notify_fail is a caught callback exception. Persistent SQLITE_BUSY/full disk is outside the finite state model and must be reported honestly by real implementation tests.
traceContract.clockDomain: Time is fixed during provider calls, response delivery, commit, notifications and crash/recovery. Only advance_time advances to the actual persisted dispatch deadline. No slow-response immediate-continuation claim.
traceContract.externalCalls: Count actual HTTP requests at a parent provider server that survives worker SIGKILL. Dead worker responses are discarded; recovery may spend a new durable budget slot. No supplier exactly-once claim.
traceContract.terminal: No new crash/recover transition is offered for an already terminal process; terminal stutter preserves projections.

fast.tlc: All five full declared finite domains must complete enumeration with zero queued states.
fast.claim: Only listed bounded depths; does not replace existing relation/knowledge verification.

deep.claim: Independent deeper report; no claim until every stage actually completes.

profileRationale: Initial cost probe for final actor-guard/synchronous-barrier model: TLC completed all five domains in 9.7-20.4s each under unchanged 60s per-check bound. Fast BMC starts at 8 steps, 6 for scripted relation concurrency, independently of full TLC. Measurements are diagnostic, not release evidence; final exact-source run remains required.
exclusions: power loss, disk-controller caches, fsync or hardware durability

manual retry or new automatic cycle
supplier exactly-once, lost-response reconciliation, notification outbox/delivery guarantees
scheduler fairness and eventual provider response
persistent storage failure guaranteed terminal settlement
time elapsing during provider/commit/recovery and slow-response immediate continuation
